title: Area and orientation under a matrix map
stem: Triangle OAB has $O=(0,0)$, $A=(4,0)$ and $B=(1,3)$. A transformation is represented by $M=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\3&-1\end{pmatrix}$. Give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the image vertices and the area of the image triangle.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Determine whether orientation is preserved, explaining your answer.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the area of the original region if its image under M has area 85.

steps.text: Apply M to each column coordinate.
Original area is 6 and $|\det M|=5$, so image area is 30.
The negative determinant reverses orientation; its magnitude gives the area scale.
Divide image area by the absolute determinant.
Original area is $85/5=17$.

title: Two orders of reflection and rotation
stem: R is an anticlockwise rotation through $\pi/2$ about O, and S is reflection in the x-axis. A point is first reflected and then rotated. Give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the matrix of the combined transformation.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the image of P=(3,1) for both possible orders.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find all points whose images are identical for both orders.

steps.text: $R=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ and $S=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$.
$RS=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$.
This is reflection in $y=x$.
Reflect then rotate gives $(1,3)$.
Rotate then reflect gives $(-1,-3)$.
Equate $(y,x)$ and $(-y,-x)$.
Only $(0,0)$ satisfies both equations.

title: Invariant directions in a stretch-shear map
stem: A map is $M=\begin{pmatrix}3&1\\0&2\end{pmatrix}$. A line through O is called invariant when each point on that line is mapped onto the same line. Give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find both invariant lines through O.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Determine the image of $(1,-1)$ after four applications.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain why an invariant line need not consist of fixed points.

steps.text: Use eigenvectors: solve $(M-\lambda I)v=0$.
For $\lambda=3$, the line is $y=0$.
For $\lambda=2$, the line is $y=-x$.
This point lies in the eigenvector direction with factor 2.
Invariant means points stay on the line, not at the same position.
Here non-zero points are multiplied by 2 or 3; only the origin is fixed.

title: Recovering a transformation from two images
stem: A linear map sends $A=(1,1)$ to $(1,4)$ and $B=(2,-1)$ to $(5,-1)$. It fixes the origin. Give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the matrix of the transformation.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the point that maps to $(7,0)$.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain why knowing the image of only one non-zero point would not generally determine a two-dimensional linear map.

steps.text: Form $M\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}1&5\\4&-1\end{pmatrix}$.
Multiply on the right by the inverse input matrix.
$M=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\1&3\end{pmatrix}$.
A 2 by 2 matrix has four entries, while one image supplies only two scalar equations.
An independent second direction is needed to determine the map uniquely.

title: Two vessels and a near miss
stem: Vessels have positions $a(t)=(2t,t)$ and $b(t)=(8,6)$ kilometres for $0\le t\le8$, with t in hours. B is anchored. Use the numerical coordinate scales shown; distance is to be calculated from the coordinates. Give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find their relative position vector and show that squared distance is $5t^2-44t+100$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the time and distance of closest approach.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the interval during which the vessels are within 2 km and explain why their plotted paths crossing would not by itself prove a collision.

steps.text: Expanding $(8-2t)^2+(6-t)^2$ gives the stated quadratic.
The quadratic has its minimum at $t=44/10=4.4$.
Minimum distance is $\sqrt{3.2}=1.78885$ km.
A collision requires the same position at the same time; here the anchored point is not on A’s line of motion.

title: A triangular panel in three dimensions
stem: A triangular panel has vertices $O=(0,0,0)$, $A=(3,1,2)$ and $B=(1,4,-1)$, measured in metres. The coordinate table is exact. Give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find a normal vector to the panel and its area.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the acute angle between the panel’s normal and the vertical vector $(0,0,1)$.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A proposed point is C=(2,1,1). Determine whether it lies in the plane of the panel.

steps.text: Compute $OA\times OB$.
A normal is $(-9,5,11)$.
Area $=\frac12\sqrt{227}=7.53326$ square metres.
$\cos\theta=11/\sqrt{227}$.
Take the dot product of OC with the normal.
$(-9,5,11)\cdot(2,1,1)=-2\ne0$, so C is not in that plane.

title: Force along a sloping cable
stem: A cable runs from O to $P=(2,1,2)$ metres. A force is $F=(6,2,3)$ newtons. Resolve F into a component parallel to the cable and a component perpendicular to it. Give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the scalar component of the force along OP.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the parallel vector and the magnitude of the perpendicular component.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain why adding the two component magnitudes does not give $|F|$.

steps.text: A unit vector along the cable is $(2,1,2)/3$.
Scalar component $F\cdot\hat u=20/3$ newtons.
Parallel vector is $(20/9)(2,1,2)$.
$|F_\perp|=\sqrt{41}/3=2.13437$ newtons.
The parallel and perpendicular components are at right angles.
Their vector sum has magnitude given by Pythagoras, not by an ordinary sum of magnitudes.
